title: Inconsistent margin above the first checkbox/toggle inside a horizontal container inside a column
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary When putting checkboxes/toggles inside a horizontal container inside a column, a `margin-top: 0.5rem` is applied to the first checkbox/toggle, and not to the others. ### Reproducible Code Example [![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-13162) ```Python import streamlit as st cols = st.columns(2) with cols[0]: st.button("Button 1", width="stretch") st.button("Button 2", width="stretch") with cols[1]: with st.container(horizontal=True): st.checkbox("Checkbox 1") st.checkbox("Checkbox 2") st.checkbox("Checkbox 3") with st.container(horizontal=True): st.checkbox("Checkbox 4") st.checkbox("Checkbox 5") st.checkbox("Checkbox 6") ``` ### Steps To Reproduce Try the above code example. ### Expected Behavior Either the `margin-top: 0.5rem` should be applied to all checkboxes/toggles, or to none. I'm not sure if the `margin-top: 0.5rem` is still worth the trouble, since we now have `vertical_alignment="center"` as well as `st.space()` to align stuff perfectly in most cases, and considering this is the second bug I've found with it (see #10265). Given that `margin-top: 0.5rem` was broken not long ago, and remains broken in this new situation, I suspect not many people would notice if we removed the `margin-top: 0.5rem` altogether. ### Current Behavior A `margin-top: 0.5rem` is applied to the first checkbox/toggle, and not to the others. ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.51.0 - Python version: 3.11.9 - Operating System: MacOS - Browser: Chrome ### Additional Information _No response_

[USER] thanks for reporting this, just want to suggest as a workaround, you could replace the columns with a horizontal + vertical containers.

This is a CSS styling bug related to checkbox/toggle margin handling inside nested layout containers. The issue occurs when checkboxes or toggles are placed inside a horizontal `st.container` that is itself inside an `st.column`. 

**Root Cause Analysis:** The bug originates in `frontend/lib/src/components/core/Block/styled-components.ts` (lines 166-171). When a column uses default vertical alignment (TOP), a CSS rule applies `marginTop: theme.spacing.sm` (0.5rem) to the first checkbox using the selector `& ${StyledElementContainer}:first-of-type > ${StyledCheckbox}`. However, when checkboxes are inside a horizontal container, the `:first-of-type` CSS selector only matches the first `StyledElementContainer` containing a checkbox within that container, causing only the first checkbox to receive the margin while others do not. This results in inconsistent vertical spacing between checkboxes in the same horizontal row.

### Related Issues

- **#10265** - Same author reported a very similar bug where the `:last-of-type` selector caused unexpected margins on the last checkbox. This is essentially the same underlying issue but manifesting differently with horizontal containers.

- **#12434** - Related alignment issue where padding on elements inside horizontal containers causes visual misalignment, showing a pattern of layout issues with horizontal containers.

- **#11207** - Related enhancement request for toggle widget layout control, indicating user needs around toggle/checkbox styling in containers.
